what_its_for: Bethanechol helps your bladder muscles squeeze and contract so you can urinate (pee) normally. It is used when your bladder is not emptying properly on its own, such as after surgery, after having a baby, or due to certain nerve problems.
how_to_take: Take bethanechol by mouth as a tablet. Always take it on an empty stomach, meaning at least 1 hour before eating or 2 hours after a meal. Taking it with food may cause nausea and vomiting. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Take it at the same times each day to keep it working consistently.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 25 to 50 mg taken 3 to 4 times a day. Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition. Do not take more or less than your doctor prescribed. Never take this medicine as a shot (injection) on your own — that form is only given by a healthcare professional.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store bethanechol tablets at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep them away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Safely dispose of any unused or expired medication.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine, as it can increase dizziness. Do not stand up too quickly, as bethanechol can cause a sudden drop in blood pressure leading to dizziness or fainting. Avoid driving or using heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you. Do not take other bladder medicines or supplements without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: sudden drop in blood pressure, fainting, severe dizziness, slow or irregular heartbeat, difficulty breathing or wheezing, chest pain or tightness, severe stomach cramps or pain, nausea or vomiting that will not stop, uncontrolled urination (leaking), blurred vision, flushing, or sweating. Also call your doctor if your symptoms do not improve after a few days of taking this medicine.
when_it_works: Bethanechol usually begins to work within 30 to 90 minutes after you take a dose. Your ability to urinate should improve fairly quickly once you start taking it regularly. Keep taking it as prescribed even if you start to feel better, unless your doctor tells you to stop.
special_populations: Older adults may be more sensitive to the side effects of bethanechol, especially dizziness and low blood pressure, so extra care is needed when standing up. This medicine is generally not recommended during pregnancy unless clearly necessary — talk to your doctor about the risks and benefits. It is not known if bethanechol passes into breast milk, so breastfeeding mothers should consult their doctor before using it. Children's dosing is determined by a doctor based on weight and condition. People with asthma, heart problems, low blood pressure, stomach ulcers, thyroid disease, Parkinson's disease, or seizure disorders should inform their doctor before taking this medicine, as it may not be safe for them.
